explanation: The L100I mutation introduces a more branched, compact side chain that subtly repositions the hydrophobic pocket geometry surrounding the NNRTI-binding site, despite maintaining equivalent van der Waals volume. Although L100I does not directly contact nevirapine (5.6 Å separation), this residue serves a critical role in defining the local conformational landscape of the fingers-palm subdomain; the isoleucine's β-branched structure creates unfavorable steric constraints that destabilize the precise protein backbone and side-chain orientations required for optimal ligand accommodation. The cumulative effect of this conformational perturbation slightly reduces binding affinity through entropic and enthalpic penalties during the induced-fit recognition process, rather than through direct molecular contact disruption.
